question:
Suppose that a particle moves in space such that its position vector at time $t$ is $\vec{r}(t) = t^2 \hat{i} + t \hat{j} + (1-t^2)\hat{k}$, $t \in [0,1]$.
(a) Find the velocity and acceleration vectors at any $t$.
(b) Find the angle between the velocity and acceleration vectors at $t = 1$.
(c) Show that the speed of the particle is maximum or minimum at $t=0$ or $t=1$ (verify using calculus), and determine which.
(d) If we select $t$ at random in $[0,1]$, what is the probability that the speed exceeds $2$?
explanation:
(a) $\vec{r}(t) = t^2\hat{i} + t\hat{j} + (1-t^2)\hat{k}$
Velocity:
$\vec{v}(t) = \frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = 2t\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 2t\hat{k}$
Acceleration:
$\vec{a}(t) = \frac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{k}$

(b) At $t=1$:
$\vec{v}(1)=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$
$\vec{a}(1)=2\hat{i}-2\hat{k}$
$\vec{v}\cdot\vec{a}=4+0+4=8$
$|\vec{v}|=3$
$|\vec{a}|=2\sqrt{2}$
$\cos\theta=\frac{8}{3\times2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{4}{3\sqrt{2}}$

(c) Speed $v(t)=|\vec{v}(t)|=\sqrt{(2t)^2+1^2+(-2t)^2}$
$=\sqrt{8t^2+1}$
$\frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{8t}{\sqrt{8t^2+1}}$
Set $\frac{dv}{dt}=0$ gives $t=0$
Check endpoints:
$v(0)=1$
$v(1)=3$
Thus speed is minimum at $t=0$ and maximum at $t=1$.

(d) $v(t)=\sqrt{8t^2+1}$
$v>2 \Rightarrow 8t^2+1>4$
$8t^2>3$
$t^2>\frac{3}{8}$
$t>\sqrt{3/8}$
Probability $=1-\sqrt{3/8}$

options.A:
(a) $\vec v(t)=t\hat i+\hat j-t\hat k$, $\vec a(t)=\hat i-\hat k$
(b) $\cos\theta=\frac{2}{3\sqrt2}$
(c) Speed is maximum at $t=0$ and minimum at $t=1$
(d) Probability $=\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}}$
options.B:
(a) $\vec v(t)=2t\hat i+\hat j-2t\hat k$, $\vec a(t)=2\hat i-2\hat k$
(b) $\cos\theta=\frac{4}{3\sqrt2}$
(c) Speed is minimum at $t=0$ and maximum at $t=1$
(d) Probability $=1-\sqrt{\frac{3}{8}}$
options.C:
(a) $\vec v(t)=2t\hat i+\hat j+2t\hat k$, $\vec a(t)=2\hat i+2\hat k$
(b) $\cos\theta=0$
(c) Speed is constant on $[0,1]$
(d) Probability $=\frac12$
options.D:
(a) $\vec v(t)=t^2\hat i+\hat j+(1-t^2)\hat k$, $\vec a(t)=2t\hat i-2t\hat k$
(b) $\cos\theta=\frac{1}{3}$
(c) Speed has maximum at $t=\frac12$
(d) Probability $=\frac14$
